morning: [laughing]Morning{you}! I've been awake for an hour and I've already sold a bucket. A bucket! To Elias, who owns three.
[happy]Good morning, sunshine. Don't look at me like that, I've had no breakfast and two ideas.
Ah, an early bird! Want to buy a worm? Freshly caught. Joking. Mostly joking.
afternoon: [laughing]Afternoon{you}! Business is slow, gossip is fast. Want the gossip? First taste is free.
[happy]Hello, hello! Come closer, I've got something to show you. It's a rock. But the STORY behind the rock!
Afternoon! You look like someone who needs a bargain. Or a hug. I sell both. The hug's free.
evening: [happy]Evening{you}! The fire's lit and I've got a brand new story. Well, an old story with a new ending.
[laughing]Ah, the golden hour! When the light makes even my merchandise look valuable.
Evening! Pull up a seat. Tonight's tale involves a goat, a duke and a very surprised baker.
night: [surprised]Out late, are we? Up to mischief? Wonderful. Count me in.
Can't sleep{you}? Neither can I. The road calls loudest at night. I'm ignoring it. Mostly.
[laughing]Shh! It's the hour of secrets. Tell me one. I'll tell you two. One might be true.

rain: [laughing]Rain! Nobody's shopping, so everyone's gossiping. My favourite weather, honestly.
Rain means umbrellas, and I happen to have three. Slightly broken. Very affordable.
[happy]I love the rain. It's the sky telling everyone to stay home and talk to each other.
clear: [happy]Sun's out! Travellers will be on the road. Customers! Strangers! Stories!
Lovely day. Perfect for selling hats. I don't have hats. Note to self: get hats.
[happy]Blue sky, warm breeze. On days like this I could walk to the coast and back. I won't. But I could.
storm: [surprised]Storm! I once rode out a storm in a hay cart with a goat named Duchess. Long story. Ask me later.
[worried]Thunder makes my stall shake. Everything's tied down except my nerves.

work: [laughing]Rearranging the stall. The trick is to put the cheap things in front and the shiny things at eye level.
Counting coins. Don't distract me. I lose count around forty and have to start again.
gather: Collecting interesting junk. One person's rubbish is another person's 'rare antique from the eastern kingdoms'.
[happy]Picking up odds and ends. You never know what someone will pay good money for. Last week: a spoon.
rest: [laughing]I'm resting. Resting my voice. Don't tell anyone, it'll ruin my reputation.
Taking a break. Even a trader has to stop talking sometimes. Very rarely. Like a comet.
socialize: [happy]At the fire! I'm the entertainment. I don't get paid, but I do get the best seat.
Lunch with the others. I'm telling Tomas about the coast. He's pretending not to listen. He's listening.
trade: [laughing]Open for business! Everything must go! Except that teapot. That teapot is my friend.
Haggling! It's not about the price. It's about the dance.
explore: [happy]Wandering. Looking for anything I can sell, or anyone I can tell a story to.
Just walking. Old habit. I like to know every path out of a place. Just in case. Not that I'm leaving.
sleep: [laughing]Mmph... if this is about the goat, it wasn't my fault... oh, it's you. Night!

tired: [sad]I'm worn out. Talked all day and sold nothing. That's like running all day and not moving.
I'm tired, but don't worry, I've still got at least one joke left. Somewhere. Let me find it.
[worried]Long night. I dreamed about the road again. Woke up not sure where I was.
worried: [worried]Business is slow. When business is slow, I get restless. When I get restless, I start packing. Help.
[worried]I owe a trader in the next valley a few coins. He's not the forgiving type. It's fine. It's fine!
Don't mind me. I'm worrying, quietly, which is very unusual for me. Enjoy it.
happy: [laughing]Best day! I sold a 'magic' pebble for a whole sack of flour. It's a pebble. It's magic now, I've decided.
[happy]I'm in a wonderful mood. Ask me anything. I'll answer honestly. Probably.
[laughing]Today everything's funny. Even Tomas. Especially Tomas.
busy: Busy, busy! Customers to charm, prices to invent. Walk and talk?
[happy]I've got a buyer coming any moment. Look natural. Look wealthy. Look like you'd pay double.

stranger: [happy]A new face! Welcome! I'm Sera, the best trader in this valley, and also the only one.
You're new? Then you don't know my prices yet. Perfect. Let's be friends before you find out.
friend: [happy]You know, you're one of the few people who laughs at my jokes. The real laugh. Not the polite one.
I'd give you a discount. A small one. A friendship discount. Don't tell anyone, they'll all want one.
close: [happy]You're my favourite person in this village. Don't tell Nia. Actually, she knows. She's okay with it.
I've told you things I've never told anyone. Even the true stories. Especially the true stories.
[happy]If I ever go back on the road, you're coming with me. I've decided. You get no say.
wary: [angry]I've been swindled by better, but never by a friend. Fix it.
I'm keeping my good stock locked up while you're around. Just so you know.

childhood: [laughing]I grew up in a river market. My mother sold fish and my father sold fishing stories. I learned from both.
When I was seven I sold my brother's boots to a traveller. He was still wearing them at the time. Long story.
I learned to count by counting coins and to read by reading the price signs. My first word was 'bargain'. Probably.
We lived on a houseboat. Every morning I woke up somewhere slightly different. I think that's why I can't sit still.
family: My mother still runs her fish stall. She's the toughest haggler alive. She once sold a fish to a man who was allergic to fish.
[happy]My father told stories so tall you needed a ladder. I got that from him. And his nose, sadly.
I've got four brothers. Four! They're all fishermen. I was the only one who wanted to see what was beyond the river.
[sad]I haven't been home in six years. I send money and silly gifts. I should go back. I keep not going.
background: I've been to fifty-two towns. I counted. I've been thrown out of nine. I'm proud of every single one.
I came here to sell a cart of pots. Mara bought one, Elias fed me, and Tomas grumbled at me. I never left.
I was supposed to stay one night. The cart broke. Mara fixed it. I 'forgot' to leave. Three years ago.
work: Trading isn't about things. It's about people. Find out what they want, and the price makes itself.
[laughing]The secret to selling is believing in what you sell. I believe in everything. That's my problem.
A good trader never cheats. Well, never cheats twice. Reputation travels faster than any cart.
I bring the world to the village. Salt from the coast, cloth from the city, stories from everywhere.
Every object has a story. My job is to tell it so well that people want to own the story.
skills: [laughing]I can haggle in four languages and insult people in seven. The insults are more useful than you'd think.
I can tell what someone will buy by the way they walk up to my stall. You, for instance: something shiny.
I can juggle three apples. Four if nobody's watching. Five once, but there were witnesses who disagree.
hobbies: [happy]I collect coins from every town I've visited. Fifty-two coins. Well, fifty-one. I spent one on a pie.
I play the fiddle. Badly. Loudly. With great feeling. The dogs howl along. That's a duet.
I write down every story I hear. One day I'll make a book. It'll be called 'Mostly True Things'.
ambitions: [happy]I want to open a proper shop here. With a sign! And a bell on the door! And customers who come back!
One day I'd like a trade road from here to the coast. Salt, fish, silk, gossip. All flowing through our village.
My real dream? Stay somewhere long enough to be part of it. I think I'm doing it. Don't jinx it.
home: My house is full of things I'm going to sell 'soon'. Some of them have been there since I arrived.
[laughing]Mara calls my house 'the cave of wonders'. Nia calls it 'a fire hazard'. They're both right.
I've got a map of everywhere I've been pinned to my wall. Every pin's a story. I'm running out of wall.
furniture: [laughing]I have seven chairs and none of them match. That's not bad taste, that's a collection.
I sleep in a hammock. Old habit from the boats. Tomas says it's 'barely furniture'. It's barely anything. I love it.
My table was made by Tomas. He gave it to me in exchange for one hour of silence. I managed forty minutes.
village: [happy]For a place this small, there's so much going on. Weddings, babies, feuds about fences. Better than any city.
This village is the only place I've ever been where people miss me when I go on a trip. That's new.
I came for one night. Now I know everybody's secrets and nobody's charged me rent. Best deal I've ever made.
friendship: Friends are the best trade there is. You give a bit, you get a bit, and both of you come out richer.
[happy]I used to make friends in every town and leave them behind. Now I keep them. It's a whole new skill.
A real friend laughs at your joke even when they've heard it before. I've tested this extensively.
disagreements: Mara still hasn't forgiven me for selling her chisel. In my defence, it looked lonely.
[laughing]Tomas and I argue about prices every week. He says I'm a thief, I say he's a miser. It's very affectionate.
Nia says my dragon scale is a fish scale. I say she's never seen a dragon. We're at a stalemate.
animals: I once owned a goat named Duchess. She ate my maps, my hat and a very important letter. I miss her terribly.
[laughing]The cats here follow me around because I smell like fish. My mother's revenge, from fifty miles away.
I'd love a parrot. One that says 'what a bargain!' every time someone walks past. Business would triple.
nature: I've seen deserts, mountains and the sea, but this valley in spring? Hard to beat. Don't tell the sea I said that.
[happy]The sea's in my blood, but I'm learning to love trees. They're like the sea, but they stay still. Mostly.
Nia keeps telling me plant facts. I've started selling them. 'Fun facts, one copper each'.
seasons: [happy]Summer's my season. Long days, lots of travellers, lots of stories.
Autumn's for harvest festivals, and festivals are for selling things to happy people.
Winter's hard for a trader. Nobody travels. I get restless. Ask me about my winter knitting. Don't.
mornings: [laughing]I'm not a morning person. I'm a morning-after-two-cups-of-tea person.
Every morning I set up the stall like it's the first day. It makes the old junk look new. Mostly.
evenings: [happy]Evenings are for the fire and the stories. I tell one, Tomas corrects it, everyone laughs.
In the evenings I count the day's coins and the day's laughs. I'm usually richer in laughs.
events: [laughing]Festivals are my favourite. I sell ribbons, sweets and 'lucky charms'. They're buttons. The luck is real, though.
[worried]When the monsters come, I hide the good stock and hand out pots and pans as weapons. Good pots, too.
When a new baby comes, I bring a little coin from my collection. For luck. And to teach them the value of money.
worries: [worried]I worry I'll get bored and leave. I don't want to. But my feet have their own opinions.
[worried]I worry I've told so many stories that people don't believe the true ones.
I worry about my mother. She's getting older and she won't stop working. Like daughter, like mother.
hopes: [happy]I hope this village becomes a market town. With festivals every season and travellers every week.
I hope I'm still here in ten years, telling the same stories to new children. That'd be a happy ending.
I'd love to take my mother to see the valley. She'd haggle with everyone. She'd love it.
surprises: [surprised]Someone bought the cursed teapot! I've been trying to sell it for two years. I almost miss it.
[surprised]Tomas laughed at one of my jokes yesterday. Out loud. I've been chasing that laugh for three years.
funny: [laughing]I once sold a man his own horse. He'd lost it the day before. He was so happy he paid double.
[laughing]I told the tinker Nia was a witch. He bought six remedies and ran. She was furious. Then she counted the coins.
[laughing]I tried to teach Elias to haggle. He ended up paying more than the asking price. Out of guilt.

mara: [laughing]Mara's the only person who's ever out-bargained me. She threatened to fix my cart wrong. I folded.
Mara acts tough, but she built me a stall roof without being asked when the rain came. Then denied it.
Don't tell Mara I said this, but she's the reason this village stands. Literally. She built it.
elias: [happy]Elias is the kindest man I've ever met, and I've met a lot of men. Most of them were trying to sell me things.
Elias overpays for everything. It breaks my heart. I keep giving him discounts he doesn't notice.
He fed me the night I arrived. Never asked for anything. I've been trying to repay him for three years.
nia: [laughing]Nia's my favourite. She's the only person who gets more excited about a weed than I do about a gold coin.
I bring Nia seeds from everywhere. She cries a little every time. It's adorable. Don't tell her I said adorable.
She's the cleverest person I know, and she has no idea. I'll tell her one day. When she's least expecting it.
tomas: [laughing]Tomas pretends he hates my stories. He's always first at the fire when I start one.
He gave me a table in exchange for an hour of silence. I didn't make it. He gave me the table anyway.
Tomas is the only person who's ever told me to slow down and meant it kindly. I'm trying. Slowly.

achievement: [laughing]You {thing}? Brilliant! I'm going to tell everyone. With extra dragons.
[happy]I heard you {thing}! That's going in my book. Chapter one, probably.
gift: [surprised]A gift? For me? I'm usually on the selling end of these! Thank you. Truly. I won't sell it. Probably.
[happy]Oh, you shouldn't have! But you did! And now I like you even more. Dangerous.
house: [happy]Your house! It's lovely. If you ever want to fill it with mismatched treasures, you know where to find me.
I walked past your house. It needs a bell on the door. I happen to sell bells.
discovery: [laughing]You found {thing}? Was there treasure? Tell me there was treasure. Tell me even if there wasn't.
Exploring! A traveller after my own heart. Next time, bring me back a story.

new_home: [laughing]A new house! With more walls for my maps and more corners for my clutter. Paradise.
I've never had a house of my own before. I keep walking round it, touching the walls. It's ridiculous. I love it.
partner: [happy]I always thought I'd travel alone. Turns out it's nicer to stay somewhere with someone.
They laugh at all my jokes. Even the bad ones. Especially the bad ones. That's love, I think.
child: [laughing]My little one already grabs at shiny things. Born trader. I couldn't be prouder.
I'm teaching my child to count with coins. They keep trying to eat the coins. Expensive lessons.
friend: [happy]I used to have a friend in every town and a home in none. Now I have friends and a home in one place.
Somebody saved me a seat at the fire last night without me asking. I nearly cried. Don't tell anyone.
grief: [sad]I don't have a funny story for this one. I just miss them.
[sad]I tell their stories now, at the fire. Somebody has to keep them alive.

stories: [laughing]Gather round! The story of Duchess the goat. You'll want to sit for this.
I was crossing the mountains with a cart of silk and a goat for company. The goat was called Duchess.
At the top of the pass, Duchess ate the silk. All of it. Then she ate my map. Then she ate my hat.
[laughing]I had to follow her down the mountain because she seemed to know the way. She did. She led me to a cheese farm. Best detour of my life.
Here's a true one. I swear on my coin collection.
In a city to the south, I accidentally sold a fake crown to a real duke.
He wore it to a ball. Someone noticed. Guards came looking for me.
[laughing]I hid in a barrel of pickled herring for six hours. I couldn't eat fish for a year. My mother was devastated.
Want to hear something I don't usually tell?
When I was sixteen, I left home without saying goodbye. I just packed a bag and walked.
My mother didn't hear from me for a whole year. When I finally wrote, she wrote back one line.
[sad]'The stall's still here. So am I.' I still have the letter. It's the only thing I've never sold.
[laughing]The story of how I came to this village. The real one.
My cart broke a wheel at the bottom of the hill. I sat on it and cursed every wheelwright ever born.
Mara walked by, looked at the wheel, fixed it in ten minutes and refused payment. Then Elias brought soup. Then Tomas told me to stop cursing near the children.
[happy]I thought, 'These people are strange.' Then I thought, 'I could stay a night.' That was three years ago.

questions.ask: If you could travel anywhere at all, where would you go?

react.sea: [happy]The sea! A person after my own heart. I'll tell you every secret of the coast.
react.mountains: Mountains? Cold, beautiful and full of goats. Watch your hat.
react.city: [laughing]The city! Noisy, smelly, wonderful. You'd be fleeced in a day. I'd come along to protect you.
react.here: [happy]Here? That's the sweetest answer I've ever heard. And the cheapest.
react.forest: The forest! Deep, quiet, full of stories. Bring a lantern. And snacks.
react.other: [laughing]{answer}? I've never been! I'll add it to the map. Then I'll make up a story about it.

questions.recall: You said you'd travel to {answer}. I found an old map with it on. Want it? For a friend price.

questions.ask: Be honest. Are you any good at haggling?

react.yes: [laughing]Oh, a rival! Good. I'll raise my prices for you specially.
react.no: [happy]Wonderful! I mean, terrible! Let me teach you. For a small fee.
react.other: That's what a good haggler would say. Very suspicious.

recall.yes: You claimed you're good at haggling. I've been watching you shop. I have notes. Many notes.
recall.no: You admitted you can't haggle. Lesson two is free. Lesson one was also free. I'm terrible at business.
recall.other: I still remember your answer about haggling. Very suspicious.

questions.ask: Tell me a secret. Any secret. I'll keep it. Probably. Actually, I will. Promise.

react.no: [laughing]A person who keeps secrets! I respect that. I'm terrible at it, but I respect it.
react.other: [surprised]Really? I won't tell a soul. Not even the cats. Your secret's safe.

questions.recall: Don't worry, I've kept your secret. Mostly from myself, I forget things.

questions.ask: Do you like stories? True ones, made-up ones, the ones in between?

react.yes: [happy]Then sit down. You're going to be here a while. Years, possibly.
react.no: [surprised]No? Everyone likes stories! You've just never heard a good one. Challenge accepted.
react.other: I'll take that as a yes. I always do.

recall.yes: You said you love stories. Good, because I've saved a new one for you.
recall.no: You said you didn't like stories. I've been working on one that'll change your mind.
recall.other: I've saved a new story for you. Whether you like it or not.
